title: SpaceX Unveils $100 Billion Louisiana Spaceport to Launch Thousands of Rockets Per Year
excerpt: The world's largest launch complex will sit on 130,000 acres of Gulf Coast land in Vermilion Parish, with construction starting in 2027 and first Starship launch targeted for 2029
body:
• SpaceX announced a $100 billion investment to build the world's largest spaceport on 130,000 acres in Vermilion Parish, Louisiana, with construction starting in 2027
  • The facility will feature 10 launch pads across five complexes, propellant production plants, a deep-water port, and its own airport — capable of more than 30 Starship launches per day
  • The project is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs and over 30,000 construction jobs, but SpaceX has yet to fly Starship to orbit or demonstrate full reusability

SpaceX has announced plans to build the world's largest spaceport in Louisiana, a $100 billion megaproject that would allow the company to launch thousands of Starship rockets per year from a sprawling Gulf Coast complex that CEO Elon Musk says will make "sci-fi real."

The new facility, dubbed "Starbase, Louisiana," will occupy approximately 130,000 acres of coastal land near Pecan Island in Vermilion Parish, on a former Exxon property about 10 hours east of SpaceX's existing Starbase complex in South Texas. Construction is set to begin in 2027, with the first Starship launch targeted for 2029.

"We're preparing to build a spaceport that, until now, has only existed in science fiction."

— Elon Musk, SpaceX CEO

A Facility Built for Scale

The Louisiana spaceport will dwarf every existing launch complex on Earth. Plans call for five launch complexes, each equipped with two pads — 10 launch pads in total. The site will also include propellant farms, an on-site natural gas processing plant to convert local gas into liquid methane fuel, deep-water shipping ports, a dedicated airport, power generation facilities, and employee housing.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ESfNkOGgbGg

Musk said the facility could eventually support more than 30 Starship launches per day, with thousands of launches possible per year. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said at the announcement event Tuesday that the company needs the additional capacity to meet its targets.

SpaceX currently operates a single working Starship launch pad at its Texas Starbase, with a second under construction. The company also launches Falcon rockets from pads at NASA's Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral in Florida, and from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

Jobs, But Questions Remain

The project is expected to create 3,000 direct jobs over 10 years, with an average annual salary of $92,600, according to Louisiana Economic Development (LED). More than 30,000 construction jobs are projected at peak buildout, and LED estimates over 8,100 indirect jobs could materialize.

Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry hailed the announcement as transformative. "With SpaceX's $100 billion investment in Louisiana, we are proving that Louisiana is open — open to new jobs, honest wages, and to those who dare to build something that lasts," Landry said.

But SpaceX's track record at its Texas Starbase raises questions. The site has been the company's most dangerous facility, with hundreds of injuries reported to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration over the past decade. In May, a construction worker employed by a third-party contractor fell to his death at the Texas site.

Starship Still Unproven at Scale

The massive investment comes even as SpaceX has yet to fly Starship — the largest and most powerful rocket ever built — into low-Earth orbit. After 13 test flights since 2023, the company has made significant progress but has not returned both the booster and upper stage to the launch pad on a single flight, a prerequisite for the full reusability that would make high-cadence launches feasible.

SpaceX has spent more than $8 billion developing Starship, according to SEC filings. The rocket is central to the company's future: launching next-generation Starlink satellites, building orbital AI data centers, and enabling missions to the Moon and Mars.

Musk recently confirmed that SpaceX will retire its Falcon rocket line once Starship reaches regular flight cadence, a signal of how much the company is betting on the new vehicle.

Environmental and Community Impact

SpaceX said it has already engaged Louisiana's Department of Wildlife and Fisheries and other state agencies to address potential environmental impacts. The company also committed to partnering with state and federal agencies on coastal restoration projects, including breakwater construction to reduce shoreline erosion.

LED offered a slightly more conservative timeline than SpaceX, projecting construction to begin by the end of 2027 with "initial operations expected to come online in 2030."
nri_angle: The massive investment could create opportunities for Indian-American engineers and aerospace professionals, with SpaceX and the broader space industry increasingly recruiting from the diaspora's deep STEM talent pool.
